application.stem: An ideal projectile begins 15 m above level ground with u_x=10 m/s and u_y=10 m/s. Take +y upward and g=10 m/s^2. Find the ground-impact time and horizontal range. Do not assume launch and landing are at the same height.
conditions: Ground is 15 m below the launch point.
The initial velocity components are already resolved.

reasoning_route.action: Use the launch point as vertical reference and mark the ground 15 m below it while retaining the gravity-only model.
reasoning_route.why_valid: The changed geometry is an event condition, not a new physical law; one reference converts the height difference into vertical displacement.
reasoning_route.output: Ground impact lies at Delta y=-15 m from launch.

reasoning_route.action: Choose Delta y=-15 m as the impact condition instead of reusing the familiar same-height condition Delta y=0.
reasoning_route.why_valid: The landing surface is below launch, so the actual geometry—not familiarity with the parent problem—determines the event condition.

reasoning_route.action: Solve the event equation and select the positive physical root t=3 s.
reasoning_route.why_valid: Only a nonnegative post-launch time can represent the stated future ground-impact event.

reasoning_route.action: Reuse t=3 s in horizontal motion to obtain Delta x=30 m.
reasoning_route.why_valid: Horizontal range and vertical ground contact describe the same impact event, so both components must share its time.

reasoning_route.action: Substitute t=3 s into vertical displacement and compare with the same-height shortcut time 2 s.
reasoning_route.why_valid: Back-substitution must reproduce -15 m, whereas 2 s reproduces Delta y=0 and therefore identifies the wrong event.
reasoning_route.output: t=3 s gives -15 m and the familiar 2 s shortcut is falsified for ground impact.

hints.text: What vertical displacement identifies ground impact relative to the launch point?
Find the physical root from the y equation, then use that same time in x.

scaffolds.text: Sketch only the launch level and ground relative to one vertical origin before writing an event equation.

transfer.statement: The learner must replace the familiar same-height condition with an unequal-height event condition and carry the resulting time across axes.

application.check: Substitution into the vertical displacement gives -15 m; the nonzero same-height time 2u_y/g=2 s is not the ground-impact time.

solution.summary: Ground impact occurs at t=3 s and the horizontal range is 30 m.
steps: Use the vertical impact condition Delta y=-15=10t-5t^2.
Solve 5t^2-10t-15=0, giving the physical root t=3 s.
Reuse t=3 s horizontally: Delta x=10(3)=30 m.
The same-height shortcut would use the wrong event condition here.

rubric.criterion: Uses the actual vertical displacement -15 m rather than a same-height shortcut.
rubric.evidence_of: Selects the event condition from geometry.

rubric.criterion: Reuses the physical impact time in the horizontal equation.

repair.action: For any unequal-height landing, use the actual Delta y=y_f-y_i in the vertical position equation and retain the actual u_y; for a horizontal launch specifically, set u_y=0, then obtain the event time vertically and share it with x.
repair.why_valid: Initial vertical velocity and landing displacement describe different facts. The landing event is fixed by the actual vertical geometry, while u_y=0 is only the horizontal-launch initial condition.
repair.output: Delta y=y_f-y_i=u_y t_event-0.5g t_event^2; for horizontal launch u_y=0; reuse the solved t_event on x
